title: Union [long, double] silently truncates a fractional value to an integer
rationale: Worse than the string case because it is arithmetic corruption rather than a type change. The LONG case calls Number.longValue(), so a Double 3.7 does not throw and the union trial loop never tries the double branch. The same failure shape the repo already fixed for BigInteger, reappearing in a different method.
catchesBugClass: Lossy numeric narrowing inside permissive union resolution - longValue/intValue/floatValue used as a conversion where a range-and-exactness check is required. The repo IntegerConverter already models the correct behaviour.
cannotCatch: Cannot catch the equivalent narrowing in the INT case unless a separate fixture puts an int branch ahead of a long branch. It also cannot catch float/double precision loss where the truncation is invisible in decimal.

predicted.detail: amount reconstructs as an integer with the fraction gone, silently, with no exception anywhere. count is included so the fixture can distinguish "truncates fractions" from "always picks long".
